# Initial Pass at updating abbreviations

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import re
import unicodedata

lex = pd.read_csv("lex_ref_link.csv", low_memory=False, dtype=str).fillna("")
abbr = pd.read_csv("lang_abbrev_master.csv", dtype=str).fillna("")

# --- helpers ---
def repair_mojibake(s: str) -> str:
    # Fix common UTF-8-as-Latin1 issues like Ã¤ -> ä
    try:
        repaired = s.encode("latin1").decode("utf-8")
        return repaired if repaired != s else s
    except Exception:
        return s

def norm(s: str) -> str:
    s = (s or "").strip().strip('"').strip("'")
    s = s.replace("\u00A0", " ")
    s = repair_mojibake(s)
    return unicodedata.normalize("NFC", s)

# --- build token -> eng_abbrev lookup (and detect collisions) ---
token_to_eng = {}
collisions = {}  # token -> set(eng_abbrev)

for _, row in abbr.iterrows():
    eng = norm(row.get("eng_abbrev", ""))
    src = row.get("source_abbrev", "")

    for tok in src.split(","):
        tok = norm(tok)
        if not tok:
            continue

        if tok in token_to_eng and token_to_eng[tok] != eng:
            collisions.setdefault(tok, set()).update([token_to_eng[tok], eng])
        else:
            token_to_eng[tok] = eng

if collisions:
    # You can print these, write them out, or raise an error
    print("WARNING: source_abbrev token collisions found (same token -> multiple eng_abbrev):")
    for t, vals in list(collisions.items())[:20]:
        print(" ", t, "->", sorted(vals))

# --- map one orig token to exactly one eng_abbrev ---
# We try:
#  1) direct lookup of normalized orig_lang_abbrev
#  2) if not found, conservative tokenization to rescue cases with extra punctuation
#     BUT we only accept it if it yields exactly ONE unique eng_abbrev.

split_re = re.compile(r"[;,/]|(?:\s+)")

def map_single_eng(orig: str):
    raw = norm(orig)
    if not raw:
        return "", "empty"

    # 1) direct match (preferred)
    if raw in token_to_eng:
        return token_to_eng[raw], ""

    # 2) conservative rescue: split on whitespace/;/,/ and also on hyphen chains
    #    Accept only if all mapped results agree (1 unique eng_abbrev).
    s = re.sub(r"[()\[\]{}]", " ", raw)
    parts = [p for p in (norm(x) for x in split_re.split(s)) if p]

    # If there's exactly one part and it's a hyphen chain, split it too
    if len(parts) == 1 and "-" in parts[0] and parts[0] not in token_to_eng:
        parts = [norm(p) for p in parts[0].split("-") if norm(p)]

    mapped = [token_to_eng[p] for p in parts if p in token_to_eng]
    uniq = sorted(set(mapped))

    if len(uniq) == 1:
        return uniq[0], ""          # success
    if len(uniq) == 0:
        return "", "unmapped"       # nothing found
    return "", "conflict"           # multiple different eng_abbrev found

# preserve the original for audit
lex["orig_lang_abbrev_raw"] = lex["orig_lang_abbrev"]

mapped = lex["orig_lang_abbrev_raw"].apply(map_single_eng)
lex["orig_lang_abbrev"] = mapped.apply(lambda x: x[0])
lex["lang_map_status"]  = mapped.apply(lambda x: x[1])

# optional: inspect problem cases
unmapped = lex.loc[lex["lang_map_status"].eq("unmapped"), "orig_lang_abbrev_raw"].value_counts().head(50)
conflict = lex.loc[lex["lang_map_status"].eq("conflict"), "orig_lang_abbrev_raw"].value_counts().head(50)

print("Top unmapped:")
print(unmapped)
print("\nTop conflicts:")
print(conflict)

# write out the cleaned file
lex.to_csv("lex_ref_link_lang_normalized.csv", index=False, encoding="utf-8")
```
```{python}
import pandas as pd
import re

# Load your normalized file
df = pd.read_csv("lex_ref_link_lang_normalized.csv", dtype=str, low_memory=False).fillna("")

# Ensure questionable exists (0/1)
if "questionable" not in df.columns:
    df["questionable"] = "0"

# Convert to int safely
df["questionable"] = pd.to_numeric(df["questionable"], errors="coerce").fillna(0).astype(int)

# Safety: you MUST have a raw column to inspect
if "orig_lang_abbrev_raw" not in df.columns:
    raise ValueError("Missing column orig_lang_abbrev_raw in normalized file. "
                     "Need the pre-normalization value to detect leading '?'.")

# Flag rows where raw abbrev indicates questionable Tocharian A/B
# (handles whitespace + case + Cyrillic В)
raw = df["orig_lang_abbrev_raw"].str.strip()

toch_q = raw.str.match(r"^\?\s*toch\.\s*[abв]\s*$", case=False, na=False)

# Set questionable=1 for those rows (do not downgrade anything)
df.loc[toch_q, "questionable"] = 1

# Optional: if you want ANY leading "?" to set questionable=1 (not just Tocharian),
# uncomment this:
# any_q = raw.str.match(r"^\?\s*\S", na=False)
# df.loc[any_q, "questionable"] = 1

# Save updated file
df.to_csv("lex_ref_link_lang_normalized_qflag.csv", index=False, encoding="utf-8")

print("Done.")
print("Rows flagged questionable (Tocharian ?):", int(toch_q.sum()))
```

# Creating separate csv with unmapped, conflicts

```{python}
import pandas as pd

# Load normalized file
df = pd.read_csv(
    "lex_ref_link_lang_normalized_qflag.csv",
    dtype=str,
    low_memory=False
).fillna("")

# Keep only conflict + unmapped rows
problematic = df[df["lang_map_status"].isin(["conflict", "unmapped"])].copy()

# Optional: sort for easier inspection
problematic = problematic.sort_values(
    by=["lang_map_status", "orig_lang_abbrev_raw"]
)

# Write out
problematic.to_csv(
    "lex_ref_link_lang_conflicts_and_unmapped.csv",
    index=False,
    encoding="utf-8"
)

print("Rows written:", len(problematic))
print(problematic["lang_map_status"].value_counts())
```

# Adding new values to qflag file.

```{python}
import pandas as pd

# --- paths (edit qflag_path to match your local file name) ---
conflicts_path = "lex_ref_link_lang_conflicts_and_unmapped.csv"
qflag_path     = "lex_ref_link_lang_normalized_qflag.csv"

# --- load ---
conflicts = pd.read_csv(conflicts_path)
qflag = pd.read_csv(qflag_path)

# --- 1) build a mapping lex_ref_link_id -> orig_lang_abbrev from conflicts/unmapped
# keep only rows where orig_lang_abbrev is actually filled
given = conflicts.copy()
given["orig_lang_abbrev"] = given["orig_lang_abbrev"].astype(str).str.strip()

given = given[
    given["orig_lang_abbrev"].notna() &
    (given["orig_lang_abbrev"] != "") &
    (given["orig_lang_abbrev"].str.lower() != "nan")
]

# if duplicates exist, "last one wins" (you can change this behavior if you want)
given = given.drop_duplicates(subset=["lex_ref_link_id"], keep="last")

map_series = given.set_index("lex_ref_link_id")["orig_lang_abbrev"]

# --- 2) fill missing orig_lang_abbrev in qflag using the mapping
# define "missing" as NaN or empty/whitespace
qflag["orig_lang_abbrev"] = qflag["orig_lang_abbrev"].astype(str)
missing = qflag["orig_lang_abbrev"].isna() | (qflag["orig_lang_abbrev"].str.strip() == "") | (qflag["orig_lang_abbrev"].str.lower() == "nan")

qflag.loc[missing, "orig_lang_abbrev"] = (
    qflag.loc[missing, "lex_ref_link_id"].map(map_series).fillna(qflag.loc[missing, "orig_lang_abbrev"])
)

# Optional: normalize back to real NaN for blanks
qflag["orig_lang_abbrev"] = qflag["orig_lang_abbrev"].replace({"": pd.NA, "nan": pd.NA, "NaN": pd.NA})

# --- 3) create a NEW conflicts_and_unmapped extract from the updated qflag
# If your pipeline uses lang_map_status, this is the safest recreation:
if "lang_map_status" in qflag.columns:
    new_conflicts_and_unmapped = qflag[qflag["lang_map_status"].isin(["conflict", "unmapped"])].copy()
else:
    # fallback: treat anything still missing as unmapped
    new_conflicts_and_unmapped = qflag[qflag["orig_lang_abbrev"].isna()].copy()

# --- 4) write outputs
qflag_out = "lex_ref_link_lang_normalized_qflag_UPDATED.csv"
conflicts_out = "lex_ref_link_lang_conflicts_and_unmapped_UPDATED.csv"

qflag.to_csv(qflag_out, index=False)
new_conflicts_and_unmapped.to_csv(conflicts_out, index=False)

print("Filled from conflicts/unmapped:", len(map_series), "unique lex_ref_link_id values")
print("Updated qflag saved to:", qflag_out)
print("New conflicts+unmapped saved to:", conflicts_out)
print("New conflicts+unmapped rows:", len(new_conflicts_and_unmapped))
```
# deleting rows w/ values in lang abbrev

```{python}
import pandas as pd

INFILE  = "lex_ref_link_lang_conflicts_and_unmapped_UPDATED.csv"
OUTFILE = "lex_ref_link_lang_conflicts_and_unmapped_UPDATED.csv"  # overwrite in place
# If you'd rather NOT overwrite, set OUTFILE = "lex_ref_link_lang_conflicts_and_unmapped_UPDATED_CLEAN.csv"

df = pd.read_csv(INFILE)

def is_missing(series: pd.Series) -> pd.Series:
    s = series.astype("string")
    s = s.str.strip()
    return s.isna() | (s == "") | (s.str.lower() == "nan")

if "orig_lang_abbrev" not in df.columns:
    raise ValueError("Column 'orig_lang_abbrev' not found in the UPDATED conflicts/unmapped file.")

before = len(df)

# Keep only rows where orig_lang_abbrev is still missing
df_clean = df[is_missing(df["orig_lang_abbrev"])].copy()

after = len(df_clean)
removed = before - after

df_clean.to_csv(OUTFILE, index=False)

print(f"Input rows:   {before}")
print(f"Output rows:  {after}")
print(f"Rows removed (had orig_lang_abbrev filled): {removed}")

```
# Multiple languages separated out

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import re
import csv

CONFLICTS_IN  = "lex_ref_link_lang_conflicts_and_unmapped_UPDATED.csv"
CONFLICTS_OUT = "lex_ref_link_lang_conflicts_and_unmapped_UPDATED_multi.csv"  # overwrite
MASTER_PATH   = "lang_abbrev_master.csv"

conf = pd.read_csv(CONFLICTS_IN)
master = pd.read_csv(MASTER_PATH)

def is_missing(series: pd.Series) -> pd.Series:
    """
    Return a pure boolean mask: True where missing/blank/'nan'.
    Avoids pd.NA in boolean ops.
    """
    s = series.astype("string")
    s = s.fillna("")              # kill <NA>
    s = s.str.strip()
    return (s == "") | (s.str.lower() == "nan")

# --- lookup: source_abbrev -> eng_abbrev ---
m = master.copy()
m["source_abbrev"] = m["source_abbrev"].astype("string").fillna("").str.strip()
m["eng_abbrev"] = m["eng_abbrev"].astype("string").fillna("").str.strip()

def norm_key(x: str) -> str:
    x = str(x).strip()
    x = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", x)
    return x.lower()

lookup = {
    norm_key(k): v
    for k, v in zip(m["source_abbrev"], m["eng_abbrev"])
    if k != "" and v != ""
}

def canonicalize_token(tok: str) -> str | None:
    t = str(tok).strip()
    if not t:
        return None

    # direct
    k0 = norm_key(t)
    if k0 in lookup:
        return lookup[k0]

    # try dot/no-dot variants
    t_nodot = t.rstrip(".")
    t_dot = t_nodot + "."
    return lookup.get(norm_key(t_dot)) or lookup.get(norm_key(t_nodot))

def format_multi_lang(raw) -> str | None:
    """
    Turn 'corn. bret.' -> 'Corn.,Bret.' using master lookup.
    Return None if not a multi-language value or mapping fails.
    """
    if raw is None:
        return None
    s = str(raw).strip()
    if not s:
        return None

    parts = re.split(r"\s+", s)
    if len(parts) < 2:
        return None

    canon = []
    for p in parts:
        c = canonicalize_token(p)
        if c:
            canon.append(c)

    # de-dupe preserving order
    seen = set()
    out = []
    for c in canon:
        if c not in seen:
            seen.add(c)
            out.append(c)

    if len(out) < 2:
        return None

    return ",".join(out)

# --- apply only to conflict rows missing orig_lang_abbrev ---
if "lang_map_status" not in conf.columns:
    raise ValueError("Expected column 'lang_map_status' in conflicts file.")

mask = (
    conf["lang_map_status"].astype("string").fillna("").str.strip().eq("conflict")
    & is_missing(conf["orig_lang_abbrev"])
)

new_vals = conf.loc[mask, "orig_lang_abbrev_raw"].apply(format_multi_lang)

# only write where we got a real string back
mask_write = mask & new_vals.notna()

conf.loc[mask_write, "orig_lang_abbrev"] = new_vals.loc[mask_write]

print("Rows updated:", int(mask_write.sum()))

conf.to_csv(CONFLICTS_OUT, index=False, quoting=csv.QUOTE_MINIMAL)

```

```{python}
unmapped_conflicts = conf.loc[mask & new_vals.isna(), "orig_lang_abbrev_raw"].value_counts().head(30)
print(unmapped_conflicts)

```
```{python}
import pandas as pd
import re
import csv

INFILE  = "lex_ref_link_lang_conflicts_and_unmapped_UPDATED.csv"
OUTFILE = "lex_ref_link_lang_conflicts_and_unmapped_UPDATED_.csv"  # overwrite

df = pd.read_csv(INFILE)

def is_missing(series: pd.Series) -> pd.Series:
    s = series.astype("string").fillna("").str.strip()
    return (s == "") | (s.str.lower() == "nan")

def norm_raw(s: str) -> str:
    # normalize whitespace so "ahd.   as." == "ahd. as."
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", str(s).strip())

# 1) YOUR manual mapping (add to this)
manual_map = {
    "ahd. as.": "OHG,OSax.",
    "as. ahd.": "OSax.,OHG",
    "ahd. mhd.": "OHG,MHG",
    "mhd. nhd.": "MHG,NHG",
    "av. ap.": "Av.,OPers.",
    "as. ags.": "OSax.,OE",
    "ags. as.": "OE,OSax.",
    "cymr. corn.": "Wel.,Corn.",
    "cymr. corn. bret.": "Wel.,Corn.,Bret.",
    "osk.-umbr.": "Osc.,Umbr.",
    "aisl. ags.": "OIce.,OE",
    "mnd. mhd.": "MLG,MHG",
    "norw. schwed.": "Norw.,Swed.",
    "schwed. norw.": "Swed.,Norw.",
    "ai. ved.": "Skt.,Ved.",
    "air. mir.": "OIr.,MIr.",
    "corn. bret.": "Corn.,Bret.",
    "ahd. nhd.": "OHG,NHG",
    "mnd. ndl.": "MLG,Du."
}

# 2) apply only to conflict rows missing orig_lang_abbrev
mask_base = (
    df["lang_map_status"].astype("string").fillna("").str.strip().eq("conflict")
    & is_missing(df["orig_lang_abbrev"])
)

raw_norm = df["orig_lang_abbrev_raw"].map(norm_raw)
mapped = raw_norm.map(manual_map)

mask_write = mask_base & mapped.notna()
df.loc[mask_write, "orig_lang_abbrev"] = mapped[mask_write]

print("Rows updated from manual_map:", int(mask_write.sum()))

# QUOTING: comma-containing values will be quoted automatically in CSV
df.to_csv(OUTFILE, index=False, quoting=csv.QUOTE_MINIMAL)

```

# add additional values

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import re
import csv

LEX_IN   = "lex_ref_link_lang_normalized_qflag_UPDATED.csv"
LEX_OUT  = "lex_ref_link_lang_normalized_qflag_MULTI_APPLIED.csv"
MATCHED  = "unmapped_multi_language_abbrevs_matched_v3.txt"

# ---------- helpers ----------
def norm_raw(s):
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", str(s).strip())

def is_missing(series: pd.Series) -> pd.Series:
    s = series.astype("string").fillna("").str.strip()
    return (s == "") | (s.str.lower() == "nan")

# ---------- load lex_ref_link ----------
lex = pd.read_csv(LEX_IN)
lex["_raw_norm"] = lex["orig_lang_abbrev_raw"].map(norm_raw)

# ---------- load matched TXT ----------
rows = []
with open(MATCHED, encoding="utf-8") as f:
    for line in f:
        line = line.rstrip("\n")
        if not line:
            continue
        # raw \t count \t "ENG,ENG"
        parts = line.split("\t")
        raw = norm_raw(parts[0])
        eng = parts[2].strip().strip('"')
        rows.append((raw, eng))

matched = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["_raw_norm", "orig_lang_abbrev"])

# de-dup just in case
matched = matched.drop_duplicates(subset=["_raw_norm"])

# ---------- merge ----------
lex = lex.merge(
    matched,
    on="_raw_norm",
    how="left",
    suffixes=("", "_from_multi")
)

mask_write = is_missing(lex["orig_lang_abbrev"]) & lex["orig_lang_abbrev_from_multi"].notna()

lex.loc[mask_write, "orig_lang_abbrev"] = lex.loc[mask_write, "orig_lang_abbrev_from_multi"]

print("Rows filled from multi-language matches:", int(mask_write.sum()))

# ---------- clean up ----------
lex = lex.drop(columns=["_raw_norm", "orig_lang_abbrev_from_multi"])

# ---------- write new lex_ref_link ----------
lex.to_csv(LEX_OUT, index=False, quoting=csv.QUOTE_MINIMAL)

print("New lex_ref_link written to:", LEX_OUT)

```
